reading.body:
CyrusOne San Antonio I publishes 9 MW of IT critical load across 110,000 square feet of technical space, yielding a density of roughly 82 watts per square foot. At 40 kW per rack as a common enterprise colocation density, this translates to approximately 225 racks, well below the footprint and power envelope of a purpose-built AI training campus. The facility holds fourteenth rank among Texas data centers with published capacity, behind 468 MW of total state capacity spread across 18 disclosed facilities.

The site holds SSAE 16, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and TIA-942 certifications, qualifying it for regulated workloads in financial services, healthcare, and government contexts. These certifications indicate a traditional enterprise colocation profile rather than the bare-metal, high-density accelerator hosting that characterizes new AI infrastructure. The operator's own facility page describes it as San Antonio's first CyrusOne enterprise colocation site, consistent with its original positioning in the product line.

Texas publishes capacity across 133 mapped facilities but only 18 with disclosed megawattage, indicating sparse transparency across the state's actual data center footprint. This facility's modest scale and regulatory-first certification stack place it outside the subset of infrastructure that currently matters to large-scale AI model training and inference. Its role is in serving established enterprise demand in a tier-two market.
